papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) inherit strong textual reasoning capabilities from their language backbones and text pretraining, but often fail to apply the same level of competency to visual inputs. We show that this degradation cannot be attributed to only perception failures, by evaluating models on semantically-equivalent text and rendered-text image inputs: models can accurately read text in the images and recover near-text performance when provided their own transcriptions, but just cannot reason well on the images directly. We characterize this discrepancy as a modality reasoning-access gap, where models fail to route perceived visual content into existing reasoning machinery accessible with text. To bridge this, we propose TIGER (Text-to-Image Gap-targeted training for Enhanced Reasoning), which first mines synthetic modality counterfactuals where a model succeeds on a text problem but fails when provided the corresponding rendered image, and post-trains the model on the image input via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), along with SFT and DPO variants. Importantly, although trained exclusively on synthetic rendered-text images with no multimodal annotations, TIGER results in model performance improvements across diverse real-world visual benchmarks including geometric diagrams (MathVerse), multi-disciplinary sciences (EMMA, MMMU), complex charts (ChartQAPro), and embodied spatial reasoning (RoboSpatial-Home). TIGER also complements existing state-of-the-art RLVR visual reasoning methods, yielding further performance gains. Analysis involving reasoning-subspace activation and activation patching provide support indicating that TIGER helps to align visual-to-reasoning pathways toward text reasoning states. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/minhngh/Tiger.

analysis.key_results: 在MathVerse、EMMA、MMMU、ChartQAPro和RoboSpatial-Home等多个真实视觉基准上取得性能提升，并能与现有最先进的RLVR视觉推理方法互补，进一步提升性能。

papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically generate actions in chunks, dividing continuous robot execution into separately predicted action chunks, which can introduce discontinuities at chunk boundaries. We propose ODEAction, a chunk-free action generation paradigm that replaces action chunk prediction with Continuous Action Evolution. We use an ordinary differential equation (ODE) to describe the continuous evolution of actions, and define the vector field of this ODE as the Action Transition Field to characterize how actions evolve with respect to evolution time. During inference, the model takes the current action as the initial condition and numerically solves the ODE defined by the learned Action Transition Field, thereby recursively generating subsequent actions with explicit dependencies. ODEAction is implemented as a modular action head that can be integrated with different vision-language backbones. Experiments on LIBERO, EBench, RoboTwin, and real-robot tasks show that, compared with action-chunk-based baselines, ODEAction improves both task performance and trajectory quality, with particularly pronounced gains on fine manipulation tasks.

analysis.key_results: 在LIBERO、EBench、RoboTwin和真实机器人任务上的实验结果表明，与基于动作块的基线方法相比，该方法在任务性能和轨迹质量上均有提升，在精细操作任务上提升尤为显著。

analysis.method: 使用常微分方程描述动作的连续演化，将ODE的向量场定义为动作转移场，推理时以当前动作为初始条件数值求解ODE，递归生成后续动作。

papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models perform versatile manipulation tasks from language instructions, but their inference cost limits how fast a robot can respond in closed-loop control. Visual token pruning reduces this cost; however, prior methods estimate token redundancy from encoded visual embeddings or attention, only after the visual encoder has processed the entire observation. We propose ActPrune, a training-free token pruning method that moves the pruning decision ahead of the vision encoder by grounding it in a geometric prior derived from the robot's own action. The action chunk predicted at the previous control step is already available before the current observation is encoded, and it specifies the end-effector and camera motion between consecutive observations. The same action affects the two standard camera views asymmetrically: in the fixed third-person view, ActPrune retains patches along the projected end-effector trajectory together with semantic anchors, while in the wrist view, it prunes patches that remain unchanged after compensating for the action-induced camera motion. Extensive experiments on two simulation environments (LIBERO and VLABench) and four real-robot tasks demonstrate that ActPrune achieves up to 1.61$\times$ speedup and 59.5% FLOPs reduction with negligible degradation in success rates. The project site is http://mmai.ewha.ac.kr/actprune/.

analysis.key_results: 在两个仿真环境（LIBERO和VLABench）和四个真实机器人任务上，实现最高1.61倍加速和59.5% FLOPs减少，成功率下降可忽略。

papers.abstract: Recent advances in robot foundation models have highlighted the potential of in-context learning (ICL) for adapting robot behavior from demonstrations without further fine-tuning. Previous work has used retrieval-based post-training to equip pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models with the capability for ICL by teaching them to condition action predictions on retrieved visually-relevant demonstration chunks. However, the effectiveness of retrieval hinges on selecting context relevant to the current execution stage, which visual similarity alone may not capture. We introduce VICTR, a framework enabling in-context learning in VLAs via progress-informed context retrieval built around an In-Context Value Function Estimator (IC-VFE). IC-VFE conditions on a reference demonstration video, a language instruction and the current observation to estimate task-relative progress. By conditioning progress estimation on a reference demonstration, IC-VFE can align the current state with a demonstrated execution even for tasks unseen during training. VICTR uses the estimated progress to select demonstration chunks at corresponding stages of execution and supplies them to a $\pi_{0.5}$ policy post-trained for in-context action generation. On unseen out-of-domain real-world manipulation tasks, VICTR raises the success rate from 6.2% for a fine-tuned $\pi_{0.5}$ baseline to 23.8% and more than doubles the task progress rate, from 28.9% to 55.5%. Project page with code, data and videos: https://ai4ce.github.io/VICTR/

analysis.key_results: 在未见过的域外真实世界操作任务上，VICTR将微调π0.5基线的成功率从6.2%提高到23.8%，任务进度率从28.9%提高到55.5%。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出VICTR框架，通过进度知情检索实现在VLA中的上下文学习，核心是上下文价值函数估计器（IC-VFE），能够估计任务相对进度并检索相关演示片段。

papers.abstract: We present Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0), a vision-language-action foundation model and embodied-agent system for stationary-base desktop manipulation. MR0 combines 147 million vision-language samples with 15,060 hours of curated robot trajectories spanning 12 embodiments. A three-stage training recipe aligns multimodal representations with robot behavior through discrete action-token pre-training, transfers these priors to continuous cross-embodiment control through flow-matching mid-training, and adapts the policy through real-world post-training. We introduce Rollback, which pairs replaced policy segments with human corrections to provide positive and negative supervision for CFG-DAgger without value learning or advantage labeling. A unified end-effector interface supports heterogeneous embodiments, while asynchronous action-chunk merging maintains smooth execution under variable inference latency. An event-driven agent maintains persistent task events and reassesses plans when progress or feasibility changes, enabling cross-task retrieval and conditional task resumption. MR0 achieves 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and ranks fifth in the RoboDojo VLA track. Under matched HG-DAgger post-training, MR0 achieves higher average success rate and progress score than $\pi_{0.5}$ across three real-robot tasks. On Ethernet insertion, CFG-DAgger trained with Rollback data reaches 70% success and a progress score of 0.90. Qualitative agent deployments demonstrate cross-task event retrieval and recovery from temporarily unsatisfied task conditions.

papers.abstract: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanWAM, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanWAM-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanWAM-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.

analysis.key_results: HumanWAM-Vanilla 经机器人后训练达到 RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean 92.08%、Clean2Random 68.88%，RoboDojo 平均成功率 14.17%、平均进度 19.00；HumanWAM-Goal 经后训练将 RoboTwin 2.0 性能提升至 Clean2Clean 92.70%、Clean2Random 84.60%，并在物理机器人上展现具身上下文学习能力。

analysis.method: 构建带手部动作和自然语言密集标注的 Open-HumanWAM-50K 视频语料库，系统性研究纯人类预训练（HumanWAM-Vanilla）和视觉目标条件的人机联合预训练（HumanWAM-Goal），并在闭环仿真与物理机器人上进行评估。

papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) enable robots to perform manipulation tasks by leveraging Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to process visual observations and language instructions. However, the action prediction objective itself lacks fine-grained task-specific perceptual supervision, making it prone to relying on task-irrelevant visual shortcuts, leading attention away from target objects and key interaction areas, thereby limiting its operational performance and generalization ability. To address this, we propose Automatic Perception-Guided Attention Alignment for Robot Manipulation ($A^3$-VLA), a framework that derives task-specific visual guidance from the manipulation process itself. Specifically, $A^3$-VLA first generates heuristic candidate regions for target objects and the robot from interaction-induced visual changes, and refines them with a visual segmentation model offline. These regions serve as explicit perceptual guidance through two complementary objectives: an attention allocation loss that encourages sufficient focus on task-critical regions when language or robot state tokens query the visual input, and a contrastive learning loss that aligns the representations of candidate target regions with language instructions while separating them from task-irrelevant regions. Extensive experiments on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that $A^3$-VLA consistently improves multiple VLA backbones, with an average success rate gain of 6.5% - 25.2% across benchmarks.

analysis.key_results: 在模拟和真实世界的操作任务上，A³-VLA能够一致改进多个VLA主干网络，平均成功率提升6.5%至25.2%。

analysis.method: 首先生成启发式候选区域，经离线视觉分割模型细化，然后通过注意力分配损失和对比学习损失对齐目标区域与指令，同时抑制无关区域。

papers.abstract: A GUI command can be correct at the interface level yet still produce an incorrect assembly. An agent must identify the relevant components, respect their structural relationships, and determine which parts should move during recovery. We introduce MAGAR-Bench, a benchmark of 4,000 multimodal samples from 26 assembly families that separates Assembly Decision, Atomic Action, and Minimal Rework. For rework, the objective counts distinct moved parts within the validated recovery candidate set for each state, rather than the number of actions. We also introduce MAGAR, a selective correction framework built on a frozen policy obtained by supervised fine-tuning. Its key design matches correction granularity to output dependencies. Structured candidates revise assembly fields and rework scope, while complete action candidates keep native GUI primitives coupled with their parameters. A learned selector retains the original prediction unless a candidate passes a task-specific intervention threshold. On recorded states from held-out assembly families, MAGAR improves Overall, the task-balanced aggregate, from 37.50 to 41.39, with gains on all three tasks. Across 209 interventions, 70 correct an error and 22 introduce one. These results support task-specific correction while highlighting the remaining tradeoff between fixing errors and preserving reliable predictions.

analysis.key_results: 在留出装配族的记录状态上，MAGAR将Overall从37.50提升到41.39，三个任务均有提升；209次干预中70次纠正错误，22次引入错误。
analysis.limitations: 摘要指出在修复错误和保留可靠预测之间存在权衡，22次干预引入错误。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出了MAGAR-Bench（包含4000个多模态样本、26个装配族，分离装配决策、原子动作和最小返工任务的基准）和MAGAR（基于冻结策略的选择性校正框架，通过结构化候选和任务特定干预阈值进行校正）。
analysis.method: 在冻结的监督微调策略上，设计匹配输出依赖关系的校正粒度：结构化候选用于修订装配字段和返工范围，完整动作候选保持GUI原语及其参数耦合；学习到的选择器除非候选通过任务特定干预阈值，否则保留原始预测。

papers.abstract: Whether an action-conditioned world model responds to actions is usually checked by replacing or removing the actions and measuring the loss in accuracy. Taking biological experiments as the guiding case, we show that such diagnostics report action effects where there are none: under autocorrelated designs, future actions stand in for history the model does not see. When the design law is known, a conditional randomization test written as an e-value is valid in finite samples whatever the model. A second failure arises whenever many sites share one action sequence, as in world models: the pooled score turns small model errors along the action contrast into an e-value near zero, so a valid test loses its power although the effect is real. Tempering the score changes the bet, not the validity. The log e-value is concave in the tempering factor and zero at zero, so too small a factor costs little and too large a one can cost everything; every single factor we tried, estimated or tuned, failed in some setting, and mixtures over a fixed grid never did. Our own preregistered analysis of optogenetic ERK experiments failed by pooling; a tempered statistic, registered before the data were obtained, then rejected the null on a never-opened field (E = 1.1e10). In three registered tests on models trained by others, the pooled test rejected in 0 of 96 units of a diffusion model, and reached the power bar in 10 of 26 Atari games under IRIS's token likelihood and 1 of 6 control tasks under TD-MPC2; mixtures fixed in advance reached it in 96 units, 24 games and 6 tasks. On recorded robot video with iVideoGPT the mixture rejected in 155 of 159 trajectories; the pooled test did not collapse there (143). Under exact nulls the statistics made 14 rejections in 26,664 tests.

analysis.key_results: 在 optogenetic ERK 实验中 E = 1.1e10；在扩散模型、Atari (IRIS)、TD-MPC2 及 iVideoGPT 机器人视频上混合方法均达到预设功效，而池化方法多未达标；在精确零假设下统计量有 14 次拒绝（共 26,664 次测试）。
analysis.main_contribution: 指出动作条件世界模型常见动作效应检验方法存在替身效应和池化放大问题，并提出使用条件随机化检验的 e 值及混合固定网格的方法来保证有效性。
analysis.method: 条件随机化检验写成 e 值，并通过 tempering 分数及混合固定网格来修正池化问题。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 本文通过生物实验类比揭示现有动作条件世界模型的动作效应诊断方法存在替身效应与池化放大问题，并提出基于条件随机化检验的修正方案。

papers.abstract: Pretrained vision language action (VLA) models show strong zero-shot performance but they are rarely deployed directly and are often first post-trained on demonstrations from the target setting. Yet VLAs are typically compared by zero-shot or full-data fine-tuned success which reveals little about the data and compute required for downstream adaptation. We study adaptation efficiency for six VLAs ($\pi_0$, $\pi_{0.5}$, and GR00T N1-N1.7) on four LIBERO suites, varying both demonstrations and training steps. This reveals differences hidden by full-data fine-tuning: models which are within two points on the full LIBERO-Spatial dataset differ by up to 3$\times$ in success with 50 demonstrations. $\pi_{0.5}$ needs 2-5$\times$ fewer demonstrations than $\pi_0$ and is the most sample-efficient model at every budget, with the largest gap on the long-horizon suite. Within GR00T, N1.5 adapts more efficiently than N1.6 and N1.7 on three of four suites, despite their stronger zero-shot performance. We also study one pretraining factor behind these differences by freezing the VLM during finetuning: this severely degrades the $\pi$ models whose VLM is jointly trained with the action expert during pretraining, but barely affects GR00T models.

papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform diverse manipulation tasks directly from visual observations and natural language instructions, but they remain prone to mistakes and unpredictable failures. Deploying these policies without continuous human supervision will require robust runtime monitors that detect when the policy has gone off-course. Existing monitors use external foundation models, such as vision-language models (VLMs) to supervise the policy, introducing significant complexity and computational cost for monitoring at runtime. In this work, we investigate an alternate approach: \textit{can a VLA's own internal activations provide the information needed to monitor its execution?} Our method trains linear probes on policy activations from demonstrations to estimate progress, then flags executions that deviate from expected progress. In experiments with the open-source VLA $\pi_{0.5}$ and across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, this approach is competitive with or outperforms VLM-based monitors in task failure detection, as well as methods which require failure data for training. These findings suggest that simple probes of VLA internals can be used to develop reliable runtime monitors, opening a path toward building policies that can act reliably and monitor their execution without external foundation models.

analysis.key_results: 在开源VLA π0.5及模拟与真实世界操作任务中，该方法在任务失败检测上优于或媲美基于VLM的监控方法以及需要失败数据训练的方法。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出并验证了一种仅利用VLA模型内部激活的轻量级运行时监控方法，无需外部视觉-语言模型或失败数据，即可在模拟与真实操作任务中达到与基于VLM的监控相当或更优的失败检测性能。

analysis.one_sentence_summary: 该工作提出利用VLA模型自身激活训练线性探测器来估计任务进展，以实现轻量级运行时监控，避免依赖外部基础模型。

papers.abstract: Vision-language-action policies may predict a transferable manipulation strategy yet fail to realize it reliably on the encountered object: objects compatible with the same grasp differ in geometry and compliance, and visual feedback degrades under closure occlusion. AgenticTactileVLA is presented as an execution-time supervisor that shifts part of object-specific adaptation from prediction to physical interaction. A fixed VLA provides the approach and hand targets; the supervisor decides whether to remain transparent, refine finger flexion, retain or release the corrected configuration, return control to the VLA for retry, or select a compliant hand-control regime. It uses finger-position and motor-effort feedback as proprioceptive contact evidence and requires neither tactile sensors nor VLA retraining. On a Unitree G1 with a BrainCo Revo2 hand, a randomized matched-block evaluation on five objects held out from VLA training yields 61.3% completion for the base VLA, 72.0% for unconditional close-to-stall control, and 84.0% for the supervisor under a shared budget; the gain is positive on every object and persists under moderate pose perturbations. Ablations show the gain is not explained by extended closure alone, and that selective triggering reduces correction episodes by 65.7% with no detected change in completion. A retention audit shows acceptance predicts retention in 88.9% of held-out cases, while compliant objects expose conservative false rejection. A thin-walled-cup study demonstrates contextual routing to compliant control, matching an always-compliant reference. These results suggest that contact-guided execution-time adaptation can improve the object-level generalization of a fixed VLA to held-out objects by adapting physical realization without object-specific retraining.

papers.abstract: World action models integrate future visual dynamics with robot action prediction, but their scalability remains limited by the need for action-annotated robot trajectories. Observation-only videos contain rich evidence about interaction dynamics, but existing approaches typically use them either to pretrain visual representations that must later be adapted for control, or to infer latent actions that are subsequently grounded to robot commands. We present NAVA-WAM, which introduces native action-prior learning by directly pretraining the action policy from observation-only videos, avoiding indirect representation-to-control transfer or a separate latent-action model. Our training consists of two stages. First, we pretrain on observation-only videos, where future-video flow-matching supervision over visual transitions is propagated through transition-structured joint attention to optimize the Action-DiT and learn action-relevant priors. Second, we use action-labeled demonstrations to post-train the Action-DiT for robot control through joint video--action flow matching, while asymmetric attention decouples the visual branch from iterative action denoising and enables efficient action-only inference. Extensive experiments show that NAVA-WAM consistently outperforms prior approaches under both in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings, while demonstrating strong action-label efficiency and effective real-robot generalization. These results establish native action-prior learning as an effective approach to directly pretrain action policies from observation-only videos, providing a scalable path beyond action-labeled robot data.

analysis.method: 两阶段训练：第一阶段在观察视频上用未来视频流匹配监督通过过渡结构联合注意力优化Action-DiT；第二阶段用动作标注演示通过联合视频-动作流匹配进行后训练，同时利用非对称注意力解耦视觉分支实现仅动作的高效推理。

papers.abstract: Generating useful robot-training data requires more than visually plausiblescenes: objects must support interaction, placements must remain physicallyvalid, and tasks must admit repeatable execution. We present\textbf{Awomo-SimDataEngine}, an agentic system that connects asset and scenegeneration to robot demonstration synthesis. Shared asset services providerigid and articulated objects, including structure-grounded part and jointgeneration with ISArt. Scene generation supports two complementary routes:Unravel reconstructs editable scenes from images, while SimForge buildssingle-room and multi-room environments from text. A graph-native harnesscoordinates construction, validation, andbounded repair, routing failures to the responsible module while retainingunaffected scene state. PolicyForge binds validated worlds to tasks and robotembodiments to produce replayable demonstrations. Evaluations cover assetgeometry, scene quality, and downstream policy learning. On MuJoCo-basedLIBERO-Plus, co-training with Isaac Sim demonstrations improves the overallsuccess rate of a World-Action Model (WAM) from $77.17\%$ to $89.43\%$. Goal and spatialsuccess improve by $31.66$ and $6.25$ percentage points, respectively . These results support the utility of the generated data for cross-simulatorpolicy training, with more limited gains on long-horizon tasks.

papers.abstract: Recent LLMs increasingly adopt hybrid designs that replace standard attention with linear attention, such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN) and Kimi Delta Attention (KDA). Although they compress the context into a fixed-size recurrent state and substantially reduce the cost of long-context processing, repeatedly reading and updating that state remains a major inference bottleneck. Quantization offers a natural way to reduce this cost, but can significantly degrade model quality, due to the accumulation of rounding errors and the presence of outlier rows and columns in the state. To address these challenges, we propose LeapQuant, a training-free method that achieves near-lossless performance under 8-bit recurrent-state quantization. First, to mitigate error accumulation, we propose per-window quantization, which leaps over a window of tokens and quantizes the state only once at its end. Within a window, outputs are computed from the fixed low-bit state together with high-precision buffered updates. Second, to reduce the error introduced by each quantization, LeapQuant retains the state's largest outliers as a few high-precision Compensator Tokens, which share the update path of real tokens. We then smooth the remaining residual before quantization to further reduce the error. Comprehensive experiments across the Qwen, Kimi, and GLM model families show that LeapQuant substantially reduces memory and compute costs during inference. With accuracy comparable to the FP32 baseline, it achieves average speedups of 2.05--3.70$\times$ at the kernel level and 1.47$\times$ for end-to-end inference on NVIDIA B200, RTX PRO 6000, and RTX 5090 GPUs.

analysis.key_results: 在Qwen、Kimi和GLM模型家族上，LeapQuant大幅减少推理时的内存和计算开销，精度与FP32基线相当，内核级平均加速2.05–3.70倍，端到端推理加速1.47倍（NVIDIA B200、RTX PRO 6000、RTX 5090 GPU）。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出LeapQuant，一种免训练的8位循环状态量化方法，通过逐窗口量化和保留少数高精度补偿器令牌，缓解误差累积和离群值影响，实现近无损性能。

papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown great promise for robotic manipulation by mapping multi-modal semantics to physical actions. However, this mapping inherently struggles to align these coarse-grained semantics with fine-grained temporal execution. It leaves VLA models with limited generalization and insufficient robustness in cluttered environments. To overcome this issue, we propose ActionUNet, an efficient multi-scale fine-tuning framework that enhances pre-trained VLA models with minimal computational cost. ActionUNet first constructs a lightweight temporal U-Net within the temporal-aligned action feature space to fuse hierarchical structural priors, effectively bridging the scale gap between semantics and temporal executions. Recognizing that multi-scale modeling can disrupt microscopic temporal continuity and cause mechanical oscillations, ActionUNet then employs a conditional SIREN as a continuous action decoder. Equipped with explicit second-order smoothness constraints, this decoder guarantees temporal continuity and reduces high-frequency motion jitter. By smoothing temporal discontinuities from multi-scale fusion, this continuous formulation reduces mechanical execution failures while preserving the base VLA model's generalization and manipulation robustness. Extensive experiments on RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks, together with real-world hard evaluations, demonstrate that ActionUNet significantly improves {\pi}0.5 success rates by absolute 9.8%, 6.1%, and 11.4%, respectively, while also generalizing to the regression-based OpenVLA-OFT backbone, highlighting its effectiveness and efficiency as a fine-tuning strategy. Code and implementation details are available at https://github.com/Di-Zhu123/ActionUNet.

papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an effective post-training paradigm for long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents. However, we find that the resulting policies can be sensitive to various policy perturbations, such as hidden-state noise, pruning, and quantization. In this work, we study how to improve perturbation robustness during policy optimization. We first introduce the notion of a perturbation robust policy and analyze conditions under which perturbed policy updates preserve stable monotonic improvement. Based on this analysis, we introduce Stable Perturbation-Robust Policy Optimization (SPrPO), which applies adaptive and sensitivity-aware perturbations during RL training. We evaluate SPrPO on ALFWorld and WebShop and conduct systematic experiments across multiple perturbation types and scales, showing improved perturbation robustness while maintaining stable policy optimization.

papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight draft model to generate multiple candidate tokens that are verified by the target model in a single forward pass. Its speedup is largely determined by the acceptance length, yet existing draft-model training methods mainly optimize cross-entropy or Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence as proxies. These objectives encourage distribution matching but do not directly optimize acceptance length, and the acceptance mechanism also differs between greedy and sampling-based decoding. In this work, we propose acceptance-length-aware training losses that directly optimize the expected number of accepted tokens within a speculative window. For greedy verification, we derive an expected accepted length (EAL) loss that explicitly maximizes expected acceptance length. For sampling-based decoding, we introduce a window total variation (WTV) loss that optimizes the overlap between temperature-scaled draft and target distributions while accounting for sequential acceptance dependencies. Both objectives can be further combined with a group-relative reinforcement learning stage (GRPO) using simulated acceptance length as the reward. Experiments across different target and draft models, tasks, and decoding settings show that our losses consistently improve acceptance length over KL-based training. WTV provides particularly strong gains under sampling-based decoding, while EAL better matches greedy verification. These results show that directly optimizing the acceptance objective, with losses tailored to the decoding mode, is more effective than conventional distribution-matching objectives.

papers.abstract: Dexterous grasp synthesis has advanced rapidly in generating stable and physically plausible hand poses, but real-world manipulation requires grasps that preserve the function implied by the task. We study open-vocabulary task-oriented dexterous grasp generation, where a robot must infer functional intent from free-form language, ground it in multi-view visual observations and object geometry, and generate an executable high-degree-of-freedom grasp. We present OpenDexGrasp, a unified data and generative modeling framework for this setting. OpenDexVerse provides dual-source supervision organized by the Coverage-to-Alignment (C2A) Recipe: OpenDex-Scale offers large-scale semantic and geometric coverage through automatic grasp synthesis and vision-language annotation, while OpenDex-Align supplies high-quality embodied alignment through human teleoperation and category-level transfer. OpenDexGrasp learns a shared perception-action latent representation that couples open-vocabulary vision-language context with dexterous action generation. Affordance grounding and grasp generation provide complementary supervision over this latent space, enabling direct generation of task-consistent dexterous grasps without a separate affordance-to-pose inference stage. Extensive simulation and real-robot experiments demonstrate improved functional alignment, physical feasibility, generalization to unseen categories, and real-world execution success. Additional details and videos are available at https://opendexgrasp.github.io/.

papers.abstract: An orthogonal rotation improves the distance rank correlation of two-bit Cohere codes from 0.75 to 0.91, yet increases nearest-neighbour comparison flips by 51%. We analyse quantization through the comparisons made by graph search. A comparison changes only when its quantization error exceeds its exact margin, giving a flip bound that separates close calls from large errors. Shared endpoints induce correlated distance errors that partly cancel within a comparison. An exact replay identity connects candidate-level actions to the output of neighbour selection. A Gaussian model gives coordinate-code errors in closed form, and a rare-spike construction exposes heavy tails in the population-radius error. Held-out blocks give model-free certificates for acceptance rules based on exact or quantized margins. Across 24 dataset-code configurations, calibration-estimated risk correlates with held-out ranking and pruning flips at 0.97 and 0.99, compared with 0.91 and 0.99 for a margin-to-noise summary and 0.74 and 0.05 for distance rank correlation. Paired builds of 200,000-vector graphs connect rotation, query scoring, and topology to end-to-end recall and search work.

papers.abstract: Procedural video-language models must solve heterogeneous tasks from the same visual evidence, including action recognition, forecasting, and procedure prediction. Dense transformer decoders share the same feed-forward networks across tasks, which can entangle task behavior and make controlled capability expansion difficult. Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) decoders provide conditional computation, but token-level learned routing is not naturally aligned with task-level procedural objectives. We propose MoTE (Mixture of Task Experts), a decoder architecture that converts large language model feed-forward networks into task-specific experts while keeping the multimodal backbone shared. Each example follows one sample-level task route, so active task-expert computation remains independent of the number of stored task experts. We instantiate this design as VideoLLM-MoTE and evaluate it on five COIN benchmarks using explicit task routes. The five-expert model activates ~2B LLM parameters per sample and achieves higher average top-1 accuracy than recent VideoLLM baselines. Under the same expert topology, it improves over dense all-expert activation and learned sparse-routing controls. These results show that task-structured routing provides an interpretable and compute-efficient decoder alternative for multi-task video-language learning.

analysis.key_results: 在五个COIN基准上，五专家模型每样本激活约2B LLM参数，平均top-1准确率超过近期VideoLLM基线；相同专家拓扑下优于密集全专家激活和可学习稀疏路由控制。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出MoTE（Mixture of Task Experts）解码器架构，将LLM的FFN转换为任务特定专家，共享多模态骨干，每个样本仅激活一个任务专家，实现计算高效且可解释的多任务视频语言学习。
analysis.method: MoTE架构：将大语言模型前馈网络划分为任务特定专家，每个样本遵循一条样本级任务路由，激活参数与存储专家数无关；实例化为VideoLLM-MoTE。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出MoTE架构，将大语言模型的前馈网络转化为任务特定专家，通过样本级任务路由实现多任务视频语言学习的计算高效解码。

papers.abstract: Federated fine-tuning of on-device large language models (LLMs) faces a significant computing burden. To overcome this limitation, split learning (SL) has emerged as a promising solution, which offloads the primary training workload to a powerful server. However, SL requires exchanging high-dimensional activations and gradients between clients and the server, resulting in prohibitive communication costs. To overcome this challenge, we propose SplitLite, a communication-efficient split federated LoRA fine-tuning method that exploits the low effective rank structure of consecutive-epoch activation and gradient residuals. Our key finding is that, under low-rank LoRA updates with the pretrained backbone frozen, the activation and gradient residuals of the same data sample between adjacent epochs exhibit low effective ranks, with most of their energy concentrated in a small number of singular directions. By exploiting this property, SplitLite transmits only quantized truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) residual factors, thereby significantly reducing both activation uplink and gradient downlink traffic. Extensive experiments on the GLUE benchmark across a series of advanced on-device LLMs demonstrate that our method reduces activation uplink communication costs by up to 93.5\% and total communication costs by up to 88.6\%, without sacrificing model performance.

analysis.key_results: 在 GLUE 基准上，激活上行通信成本最高降低 93.5%，总通信成本最高降低 88.6%，且不牺牲模型性能。
analysis.main_contribution: 利用连续 epoch 激活和梯度残差的低有效秩结构，仅传输量化截断 SVD 残差因子，大幅降低分割学习中的通信成本。
analysis.method: 将激活和梯度残差进行截断奇异值分解并量化，仅传输量化后的低秩因子。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出 SplitLite，一种通信高效的分割联邦 LoRA 微调方法，利用连续 epoch 激活和梯度残差的低有效秩结构来压缩通信。

papers.abstract: When the weights and biases of a neural network range over a fixed finite alphabet, training the network to fit a data set exactly becomes a finite combinatorial problem, and parameterized complexity asks which structural quantities of an instance make this problem tractable. Ganian, Sommer, and Sorge (ICLR 2026) showed that training quantized networks is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized jointly by the input dimension $\alpha$, the output dimension $\omega$, and the treewidth of the architecture, and they asked whether $\alpha+\omega$ alone suffices. We show that it does not: training binary quantized networks is W[1]-hard parameterized by $\alpha+\omega$, so it admits no algorithm with running time $f(\alpha+\omega)\cdot|I|^{O(1)}$ for any computable $f$ unless FPT = W[1]. Hardness holds already for exact fitting of $k+1$ examples whose inputs equal their targets and form a coordinatewise prefix chain, and also when all biases are fixed to zero. The proof rests on a one-flip routing equivalence. On such data, nonnegative binary weights force every neuron to switch on at most once, and a network fits the data exactly if and only if the architecture contains vertex-disjoint paths that link each changing input to the corresponding output. Every neuron therefore has one of only $k+1$ activation profiles, yet deciding whether these profiles can be realized simultaneously is as hard as disjoint-path routing. Small input and output dimensions thus limit what each neuron can do locally, but not how the architecture forces neurons to share resources globally.

analysis.key_results: 训练二进制量化网络在参数 α+ω 下是 W[1]-难的，除非 FPT=W[1]，不存在运行时间为 f(α+ω)·|I|^{O(1)} 的算法；硬度结果在偏置固定为零时依然成立。
analysis.main_contribution: 证明了二进制量化神经网络训练在参数为输入维度与输出维度之和时是 W[1]-难的，从而否定了现有固定参数可解结论仅用这两项参数的可能性。
analysis.method: 通过构造输入等于目标且形成坐标前缀链的特定数据集，并证明网络精确拟合当且仅当网络架构中存在连接每个变化输入到对应输出的顶点不相交路径（one-flip routing equivalence），从而归约到不相交路径路由问题。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 该论文证明训练二进制量化神经网络在仅以输入和输出维度为参数时是 W[1]-难的，解决了先前工作中关于参数化复杂性的遗留问题。

papers.abstract: Modern LLM deployments use a number of implementation choices and inference optimizations (e.g., batching, custom kernels, and quantization) on top of fixed weights, so two engines serving "the same model" can produce meaningfully different distributions. We study the problem of estimating the total variation (TV) distance between two length-$n$ autoregressive distributions to additive error $\varepsilon$, under three access models. (1) Under sample access, we use $\widetilde{O}(n^2 K/\varepsilon^2)$ queries, where $K$ is the maximum support of the next-token distribution. This improves upon the $\widetilde{O}(n^3 m/\varepsilon^5)$-query estimator of Meel et al. (2025), where $m \geq K$ is the total size of the token alphabet. (2) Under logit access, we use $O(n/\varepsilon^2)$ queries, and this is tight. (3) Under noisy logit access, we smoothly interpolate between the above two guarantees: if probability values are given to relative error $\sigma$, we use $\widetilde{O}((n+n^2\sigma^2)/\varepsilon^2)$ queries. We complement our theoretical results with an empirical evaluation of our algorithms, for example measuring the distance between SGLang and vLLM serving identical weights. Our experiments highlight the robustness and practicality of estimating the total variation distance, which remains estimable where the KL divergence is infinite. Our code is available at https://github.com/XunZhiyang/llm-tv-estimation.

analysis.key_results: 样本访问下查询复杂度为O(n^2 K/ε^2)，logit访问下为O(n/ε^2)且最优，噪声logit访问下为O((n+n^2σ^2)/ε^2)；实证比较了SGLang和vLLM的分布差异。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出了在样本访问、logit访问和噪声logit访问下估计自回归分布总变差距离的新算法，改进了查询复杂度并给出紧界。

papers.abstract: The paper presents a voice anonymization model focusing on preserving content rather than producing realistic speech. It relies on content embeddings extracted from a frozen pretrained wav2vec2 encoder. These embeddings are decoded into an anonymized signal using vector quantization and a HiFi-GAN vocoder, both trained on LibriTTS without any waveform reconstruction loss or speaker embedding mapping. The training objective enforces that embeddings of the anonymized signal match those of the original one. While training, an auxiliary speaker classification branch with a gradient reversal layer is used to discard speakerspecific information. Results show that this straightforward embedding-based approach achieves very low WER (2.53) with an anonymization performance (EER 13.39) ranking within first level for VPC. Notably, emotions are partially preserved (UAR 43.91), even without a supporting training objective, while the anonymized voice is audible without reconstruction loss.

analysis.key_results: WER 2.53，EER 13.39，情绪识别 UAR 43.91，在 VPC 中匿名化性能处于第一梯队。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出一种基于内容嵌入匹配的语音匿名化方法，使用向量量化和 HiFi-GAN 解码内容嵌入，训练目标为匿名信号嵌入与原始信号嵌入匹配，并通过梯度反转层去除说话人信息。
analysis.method: 利用冻结的 wav2vec2 编码器提取内容嵌入，使用向量量化和 HiFi-GAN 声码器生成匿名语音，训练时嵌入匹配损失，辅助说话人分类分支带梯度反转层。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 本文提出一种基于冻结的 wav2vec2 内容嵌入的语音匿名化模型，通过向量量化编码器与 HiFi-GAN 声码器直接重建匿名语音，无需波形重建损失或说话人映射。

papers.abstract: How can richer training supervision improve robot control while keeping the deployed policy compact? We present XS-VLA, a staged training framework using teacher-derived spatial labels and demonstration-conditioned action learning. Coarse-Grained Spatial Distillation (CSD) initializes the backbone through an auxiliary region-label task. Latent Flow Matching (LFM) then conditions an action-space velocity field on a demonstration latent, using KL regularization while jointly optimizing the backbone and action modules. The deployed policy contains 243.99M parameters and operates without the teacher or posterior encoder. XS-VLA achieves 90.25% average LIBERO success in each of two training seeds, compared with 86.00% for a SmolVLA-0.25B base trained under our settings. Ablations examine both training stages through matched image pretraining and Huber/MSE controls. On three Mobile ALOHA tasks, average strict success increases from 21.7% to 65.0%. These results demonstrate the control utility of auxiliary representation initialization and regularized demonstration-conditioned flow learning for compact VLA policies

analysis.key_results: 在LIBERO基准上，两次训练种子平均成功率达到90.25%，高于相同设置下SmolVLA-0.25B基线的86.00%；在三个Mobile ALOHA任务上，平均严格成功率从21.7%提升至65.0%；消融实验验证了两个训练阶段的作用。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出XS-VLA分阶段训练框架，包含粗粒度空间蒸馏（CSD）初始化骨干网络和潜流匹配（LFM）以演示潜变量为条件的动作生成，在不依赖教师或后验编码器的情况下实现紧凑VLA策略。
analysis.method: Coarse-Grained Spatial Distillation (CSD)：利用辅助区域标签任务初始化骨干网络；Latent Flow Matching (LFM)：以演示潜变量为条件在动作空间速度场上进行训练，并使用KL正则化联合优化骨干和动作模块；部署策略参数量为243.99M，推理时不使用教师或后验编码器。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出一种分阶段训练框架，通过教师派生的空间标签和演示条件动作学习，在保持部署策略紧凑的同时提升机器人控制性能。

papers.abstract: INT2 KV-cache quantization is attractive for long-context LLM serving, yet making it both accurate and practical remains challenging. Data-oblivious rotations such as Hadamard transforms flatten channel outliers, but still degrade sharply at INT2 because they ignore how downstream attention queries the cache. We propose OSCAR, an ultra-low-bit KV-cache quantization method that estimates attention-aware covariance targets offline and uses them to derive fixed per-layer rotations and clipping thresholds. By aligning the quantization basis with the second-moment structures consumed by attention, OSCAR preserves attention fidelity at 2-bit precision. Beyond theoretical analysis under a frozen-error surrogate, we build a serving-ready OSCAR system with fused Triton write and decode kernels that preserve paged KV-cache layouts and prefix caching, integrating into modern serving engines such as SGLang and vLLM. We evaluate OSCAR on reasoning and coding benchmarks with generation traces of up to 32K tokens across five tasks. On Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 and Qwen3-8B, OSCAR narrows the BF16 accuracy gap to 3.78 and 1.21 points, respectively, where Hadamard-only INT2 collapses, and matches BF16 within run-to-run variance on Qwen3-32B and GLM-4.7 (358B parameters). On RULER-NIAH up to 128K tokens, OSCAR substantially outperforms QuaRot-style INT2 across context lengths. System-wise, OSCAR compresses KV-cache memory by nearly $8\times$, boosts multi-request throughput by up to $7.8\times$ at large batch sizes within the same memory budget, and accelerates batch-size-1 decoding by up to $3.1\times$ over BF16 by cutting KV memory traffic.

analysis.key_results: 在Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507和Qwen3-8B上，OSCAR将BF16精度差距分别缩小到3.78和1.21个点，而仅Hadamard的INT2量化失效；在Qwen3-32B和GLM-4.7（358B参数）上与BF16的差异在运行间方差内；在RULER-NIAH上（最长128K token）显著优于QuaRot风格INT2；系统方面，KV缓存内存压缩近8倍，大批次多请求吞吐量提升高达7.8倍，批大小为1的解码速度提升高达3.1倍。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出OSCAR，一种超低比特KV缓存量化方法，通过离线估计注意力感知协方差目标，推导出固定逐层旋转和裁剪阈值，在2比特精度下保持注意力保真度，并构建了集成到SGLang和vLLM中的服务就绪系统。
analysis.method: 离线估计注意力感知协方差目标，利用这些目标推导出固定的逐层旋转和裁剪阈值，使量化基与注意力消费的二阶矩结构对齐；并采用融合的Triton写入和解码内核，保留分页KV缓存布局和前缀缓存。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 本文提出OSCAR，一种利用离线估计的注意力感知协方差目标来生成固定逐层旋转和裁剪阈值的2比特KV缓存量化方法，以在长上下文LLM服务中保持注意力保真度。

papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are effective as end-to-end motion planners, but can be brittle when evaluated in closed-loop settings due to being trained under traditional imitation learning framework. Existing closed-loop supervision approaches lack scalability and fail to completely model a reactive environment. We propose MAPLE, a novel framework for reactive, multi-agent rollout of a dynamic driving scenario in the latent space of the VLA model. The ego vehicle and nearby traffic agents are independently controlled over multi-step horizons, while being reactive to other agents in the scene, enabling closed-loop training. MAPLE consists of two training stages: (1) supervised fine-tuning on the latent rollouts based on ground-truth trajectories, followed by (2) reinforcement learning with global and agent -specific rewards that encourage safety, progress, and interaction realism. We further propose diversity rewards that encourage the model to generate planning behaviors that may not be present in logged driving data. Notably, our closed-loop training framework is scalable and does not require external simulators, which can be computationally expensive to run and have limited visual fidelity to the real-world. MAPLE achieves state-of-the-art driving performance on Bench2Drive and demonstrates scalable, closed-loop multi-agent play for robust E2E autonomous driving systems.

analysis.key_results: 在Bench2Drive上达到最先进的驾驶性能，并展示了可扩展的闭环多智能体博弈。

analysis.method: 两阶段训练：(1) 基于真实轨迹的隐空间rollout监督微调；(2) 使用全局与智能体特定奖励的强化学习，并引入多样性奖励鼓励生成规划行为。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出MAPLE框架，在VLA模型的隐空间中进行多智能体反应式闭环训练，以提升端到端自动驾驶的鲁棒性。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 直接以VLA模型为训练核心，在隐空间中进行闭环多智能体训练，对VLA在端到端自动驾驶中的鲁棒性和可扩展性有重要贡献。

papers.abstract: Quantization has become a standard tool for efficient LLM deployment, especially for local inference, where models are now routinely served at 2-3 bits per parameter. The state of the art is currently split into simple scalar quantization techniques, such as GPTQ or AWQ, which are widely deployed but plateau in accuracy at 3-4 bits per parameter (bpp), and "second-generation" vector- or trellis-quantized methods, such as QTIP, GPTVQ and AQLM, which push the accuracy frontier but are notoriously hard to implement and to scale. In this paper, we ask whether this gap is fundamental, or whether a carefully optimized $\textit{scalar}$ quantizer can recover most of it. We answer in the affirmative, by introducing GSQ (Gumbel-Softmax Quantization), a post-training scalar quantization method which jointly learns the per-coordinate grid assignments and the per-group scales using a Gumbel-Softmax relaxation of the discrete grid. GSQ matches the cardinality of the relaxation to the small number of levels available in the target bit-width regime (e.g., 3-8 levels for ternary and 3 bpp, respectively), making optimization tractable. Practically, on the standard Llama-3.1-8B/70B-Instruct models, GSQ closes most of the gap between scalar quantization and the QTIP frontier at 2 and 3 bits, while using a symmetric scalar grid with group-wise quantization, and thus remains compatible with existing scalar inference kernels. We further show that the same discrete-assignment optimization can be applied to practical GGUF K-Quant checkpoints: starting from publicly released GGUF models, GSQ improves accuracy while projecting the result back into the same deployment format. Finally, GSQ scales to trillion-scale Mixture-of-Experts models such as Kimi-K2.5, where vector-quantized methods are difficult to apply. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/IST-DASLab/GSQ.

analysis.key_results: 在Llama-3.1-8B/70B-Instruct模型上，GSQ在2和3比特下消除了标量量化与QTIP前沿之间的大部分差距；可应用于GGUF K-Quant检查点并转换回相同部署格式；扩展到万亿级MoE模型Kimi-K2.5。

analysis.method: 使用Gumbel-Softmax松弛离散网格，匹配目标比特宽度下可用级别数量，联合优化每坐标网格分配和每组尺度。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 本文提出GSQ，一种基于Gumbel-Softmax松弛的后训练标量量化方法，可在2-3比特下显著缩小标量量化与矢量量化前沿方法之间的精度差距。

papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models ground natural-language instructions in visual observations to generate actions for robotic manipulation. On long-horizon tasks, existing VLA models face structure-blind backbones, backbone-bound generalization, and flat single-objective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Neuro-Symbolic Vision-Language-Action (NS-VLA) framework. It introduces a Neuro-Symbolic Encoder that parses the instruction into a primitive plan tracked by a gated monotone stage pointer, a Neuro-Symbolic Solver that conditions a chunked VLA policy on the active sub-instruction, and Hierarchical Joint Policy Optimization, which fits the pointer on demonstration segments and refines the action policy with success-filtered online learning. Even when trained on few demonstrations, NS-VLA clearly leads on LIBERO and the held-out LIBERO-Plus (76.5% and 51.8% against 71.2% and 45.4% for its backbone), exceeds the strongest baseline by 12.7 points on long-horizon tasks, and raises real-robot success from 40.0% to 60.0%. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Zuzuzzy/NS-VLA.

papers.abstract: Despite remarkable progress in Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) for robot manipulation, these large pre-trained models require fine-tuning to be deployed in specific environments. These fine-tuned models are highly sensitive to camera viewpoint changes that frequently occur in unstructured environments. In this paper, we propose a zero-shot camera adaptation framework without additional demonstration data, policy fine-tuning, or architectural modification. Our key idea is to virtually adjust test-time camera observations to match the training camera configuration in real-time. For that, we use a recent feed-forward novel view synthesis model which outputs high-quality target view images, handling both extrinsic and intrinsic parameters. This plug-and-play approach preserves the pre-trained capabilities of VLAs and applies to any RGB-based policy. Through extensive experiments on the LIBERO benchmark, our method consistently outperforms baselines that use data augmentation for policy fine-tuning or additional 3D-aware features for visual input. We further validate that our approach constantly enhances viewpoint robustness in real-world robotic manipulation scenarios, including settings with varying camera extrinsics, intrinsics, and freely moving handheld cameras. Project Page: https://heo0224.github.io/AnyCamVLA/

papers.abstract: Despite advances in vision-language-action (VLA) models, they remain limited in highly dynamic game settings such as 3D open worlds and competitive player versus player (PvP) settings, where agents must efficiently extract sparse, actionable signals from dense visual input while integrating multimodal cues to track off-screen high-value targets in real time. To address this, we introduce 3A-VLA (Abstraction-Aligned Action VLA), a framework that grounds action learning in explicit intention and environment abstractions rather than superficial pattern matching. We introduce dual task-agnostic abstractions: the intention abstraction (IA), which condenses verbose instructions and reasoning into explicit semantic primitives, and the environment semantics abstraction (ESA), which structures dense visual streams into a spatial-functional affordance representation to guide grounded actions. We further propose an abstraction alignment reweighting (AAR) module that adaptively reweights the action imitation loss. A continuous intention-environment alignment signal is used to emphasize reliable action supervision when abstractions agree and reduce the influence of ambiguous demonstrations when they diverge, thereby learning a policy that balances fine-grained control and high-level reasoning without the need for manual rules. Extensive experiments show that 3A-VLA performs competitively among the evaluated baselines in both open-world (Minecraft) and competitive PvP (Game for Peace) settings. It also demonstrates zero-shot combat transfer from Game for Peace to high-fidelity games, including Valorant, CS2, GTA V, Elden Ring, and Mount & Blade.

analysis.key_results: 在Minecraft和Game for Peace中表现具有竞争力，并展示了从Game for Peace到Valorant、CS2、GTA V、Elden Ring和Mount & Blade的零样本战斗迁移能力。

analysis.method: 采用双重任务无关抽象（意图抽象IA和环境语义抽象ESA），并结合抽象对齐重加权（AAR）模块，利用连续的意图-环境对齐信号来强调可靠的动作监督。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 3A-VLA通过意图抽象和环境语义抽象对齐，提升视觉语言动作模型在3D游戏世界中的行动学习能力。

(i) When trained on action sequences such as “move left, aim, shoot,” the model learns the semantic relationship between “wall” and “move left,” recognizing the object’s functional role as tactical cover rather than merely its presence. (ii) When tasked with locating off-screen enemies, the model uses the structured affordance representation from the ESA to reason about likely ambush points, such as inferring that a “wall” may serve as high-probability cover from which an opponent could emerge, thereby enabling proactive searches. papers.abstract: Early-exit (EE) LLMs let confident tokens skip a model's deep layers, but batched serving loses most of this gain. Current systems either force tokens to exit before their own ramp is confident, an error the ramp does not bound, or save almost nothing when decoding is weight-bound, because any continuing token makes a step read the deep weights. We present DREX, a batched EE serving system that never forces a token to exit. DREX introduces cross-iteration batching: tokens that continue past the exit layer wait there, and every few steps one deep pass over all waiting tokens reads the deep weights once for several steps. Its two policies differ in what such a token's request does: holding pauses it until the deep pass, and speculative holding lets it keep decoding from the exit layer's own guess, which the next deep pass verifies. Exited tokens are trusted and never verified. Using a calibrated cost model, a controller picks speculative holding where reading weights dominates a step and guesses are often right, and holding elsewhere. DREX keeps vLLM's asynchronous scheduling by planning each deep pass from exit counts of earlier steps. With synthetic exits where 90% of tokens exit at a quarter of the depth and 40% of guesses are correct, DREX achieves 2.22-2.24$\times$ decode speedup over non-EE across batch sizes on Llama-2-70B, while per-row skipping (vSkipper's design) gains at most 7.0%. On LayerSkip models, DREX adds no statistically resolved quality loss to the EE model's own. On CNN/DM at full memory, DREX with LayerSkip achieves 1.58-1.91$\times$ decode speedup while remaining within 1.4 ROUGE-2 points of the non-EE model. These speedups are 9-63% larger than EAGLE's across the evaluated model sizes, with each method measured against its own non-EE target.

papers.abstract: % Waiting until a driving hazard becomes directly visible can leave an autonomous vehicle little time to respond. Observable precursors, such as another vehicle's unexpected braking, can provide evidence of a hidden hazard and an opportunity for earlier risk mitigation. However, existing driving datasets and language reasoning formulations provide limited supervision for connecting these precursors to potential risks and appropriate responses. We introduce PotentialRiskQA, an ego-view driving dataset that marks precursor and risk appearance times and provides structured annotations linking scene evidence, potential risks, and mitigation actions. Building on this dataset, PR-Reasoner trains vision-language models to generate a precursor-centered reasoning chain through scene-level supervision and auxiliary tasks for scene understanding, precursor identification, risk inference, driving suggestions, and meta-actions. Experiments across multiple backbones show improved scene understanding, risk cognition, and action quality, with fewer unsupported risk claims on most models. Ablations show that supervising intermediate reasoning steps further reduces unsupported risk claims and improves action quality beyond scene-level training alone. On NAVSIM, the trained representations improve open-loop planning performance, demonstrating benefits beyond language-based evaluation.

papers.abstract: Transformers replace recurrence with a memory that grows with sequence length and self-attention that enables ad-hoc lookups over past tokens. Consequently, they lack an inherent incentive to compress history into compact latent states with consistent transition rules. This often leads to learning solutions that generalize poorly. We introduce Next-Latent Prediction (NextLat), which extends standard next-token training with self-supervised predictions in the latent space. Specifically, NextLat trains a transformer to learn latent representations that are predictive of its next latent state given the next token. Theoretically, we show that these latents converge towards belief states, compressed information about the history necessary to predict the future. This simple auxiliary objective injects a recurrent inductive bias into transformers while leaving their architecture, parallel training efficiency, and inference unchanged. NextLat effectively encourages transformers to form compact internal world models with coherent belief states and transition dynamics -- crucial properties not guaranteed by standard next-token prediction alone. Empirically, across benchmarks in world modeling, reasoning, planning, and language modeling, NextLat demonstrates significant gains over standard next-token prediction and other baselines in downstream accuracy, representation compression, and lookahead planning. Furthermore, NextLat enables variable-length self-speculative decoding, accelerating inference by up to 3.3x in language modeling. NextLat offers a simple yet effective paradigm for learning compact, predictive representations in transformers that generalize better. Our code is available at https://github.com/JaydenTeoh/NextLat.

analysis.key_results: 在多个世界建模、推理、规划和语言建模基准上显著优于标准下一token预测和其他基线；推理速度最高提升3.3倍（语言建模中的可变长度自推测解码）。

papers.abstract: Verifiers--functions assigning rewards to agent behavior--have been key to AI progress in math, code, and games. However, extending gains to domains without clear-cut success criteria (e.g., computer use) remains a challenge: while humans can recognize desired outcomes, translating this intuition into scalable rules is nontrivial. Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) offer a promising solution, given their world knowledge, human-preference alignment, and reasoning skills. We evaluate MLLM verifiers across web navigation, computer use, and robotics, spanning 13 models, 28 judge designs, diverse agent trajectories, and distinct downstream applications. We identify a critical limitation: a strong tendency for MLLMs to over-validate agent behavior, a phenomenon we term agreement bias. This bias is pervasive across models, is resilient to test-time scaling, and harms pipelines relying on MLLM judgments (e.g., self-improvement). We discuss principles for design and evaluation of verifiers, and introduce SGV, a method that improves verification by harnessing MLLMs' own capabilities via modulation of (un)conditional generation. First, an MLLM generates broad priors about desired behavior, independent of the data under evaluation. Then, conditioned on generated priors, it reasons over and judges a candidate trajectory. Our methods yield more human-aligned verifiers, with gains of up to 25pp in failure detection, 14pp in accuracy, and benefits extending to downstream applications. In self-improvement and online supervision, our verifiers boost task completion of a GUI specialist in OSWorld, a diffusion policy in robomimic, and a ReAct agent in VisualWebArena--surpassing the previous SOTA by 20pp. Finally, we release an updated version of VisualWebArena, featuring improved evaluators, high-fidelity environment parallelism with >10x speedups, and VWA-Lite, a 1/3-scale subset with comparable evaluation fidelity.

papers.abstract: Weight binarization has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce the complexity of large language models (LLMs). Existing approaches fall into post-training binarization, which is simple but causes severe performance loss, and training-aware methods, which depend on full-precision latent weights, adding complexity and limiting efficiency. We propose a novel framework that represents LLMs with multi-kernel Boolean parameters and, for the first time, enables direct finetuning LMMs in the Boolean domain, eliminating the need for latent weights. This enhances representational capacity and dramatically reduces complexity during both finetuning and inference. Extensive experiments across diverse LLMs show our method outperforms recent ultra low-bit quantization and binarization techniques.
